business_problem: NIO's autonomous-driving program was generating tens of petabytes of data, and growing vehicle-data ingestion plus training-platform access frequency was making public-cloud network and storage costs, efficiency, and compliance constraints increasingly hard to manage.
solution_summary: NIO used Tencent Cloud's distributed storage stack to build a private-cloud foundation for autonomous-driving data instead of keeping all data on public-cloud storage. TStor OneCOS massive object storage is the core layer, giving NIO a data-lake and data-center storage base that can scale to trillions of objects and rapid capacity growth. Tencent paired OneCOS with GooseFS so data preparation, model training, inference, and small-file or HDFS-style access could run faster against the same shared pool. YottaStore provides the distributed storage engine with EC 8+4 redundancy, log cache, automatic balancing, and repair, while StarLake servers provide the dense hardware used to scale the platform into the hundreds of petabytes. The result is a hybrid/private storage environment for sensitive data, AI workloads, and lower-cost expansion.

solution_components.name: TStor OneCOS massive object storage
solution_components.role: Acts as the private-cloud object storage and data-lake foundation for autonomous-driving datasets.

solution_components.name: GooseFS
solution_components.role: Accelerates small-file, HDFS-style, and nearby data access for data preparation, model training, and inference workflows.

solution_components.name: YottaStore distributed storage
solution_components.role: Provides the underlying distributed storage engine, redundancy, balancing, and repair mechanisms for the storage pool.

solution_components.name: StarLake server
solution_components.role: Supplies the dense server foundation used to assemble the hundreds-of-petabytes storage pool.

data_flow: Vehicle data and training-platform datasets land in TStor OneCOS, where YottaStore manages durability and cluster balancing. GooseFS then accelerates small-file and HDFS-style access so data preparation, model training, and inference can work against the shared storage pool, while StarLake servers provide the dense hardware layer that scales the environment to hundreds of petabytes.
business_outcome: NIO met autonomous-driving capacity, performance, compliance, and cost targets with a private-cloud storage platform that supports rapid data growth, EB-scale planning, faster AI-data access, and materially lower hardware spending.
metrics: NIO had already been using public cloud storage for tens of petabytes of data.
The platform supports 1 trillion+ file indexes.
It supports 1 million+ request QPS access.
The architecture targets 12 nines of reliability.
Hardware resource cost is reduced by more than 50%.
architecture_clues: Sensitive data is stored in a local data center for compliance requirements.
Tencent describes the storage layer as suitable for private and hybrid cloud deployments.
EC 8+4 redundancy is used to balance space utilization and reliability.
The storage pool scales to hundreds of petabytes and is intended to support future L4/L5 autonomous-driving models.
